Magnus Ericsson. Source: Luleå University of Technology
Posted By: Adrian Pocobelli October 7, 2026
This week’s episode features Magnus Ericsson , adjunct professor at Luleå University of Technology in Sweden and co-founder of Mineral Economics and the Raw Materials Report, in conversation with host Adrian Pocobelli on the history of rare earths.
Ericsson explains how rare earths were first discovered and how investment by the Swedish monarchy in scientific research helped create the conditions for a series of important discoveries in Sweden, including several rare earth elements as well as nickel and cobalt. He also discusses the origins of the unusual names given to many rare earths and explores the feedback loop between science, technology, and metals, in which advances in one field help drive progress in the others.
All this and more with host Adrian Pocobelli.
This week’s Spotlight features Novo Resources executive co-chairman Mike Spreadborough, who discusses the company’s exploration projects in Australia. To learn more, visit: https://novoresources.com/
